rows.text: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
In the real economy, while exports continue to show steady growth, facilities and construction investment maintain robust paces of increase, and private consumption appears to be recovering.
Meanwhile, the current account has recorded a deficit recently owing mainly to the narrowed goods account surplus and the repatriation of dividends.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
Consumer price inflation and core inflation both remain stable.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
In the real economy, while exports continue to show steady growth, facilities and construction investment maintain robust paces of increase, and private consumption appears to be recovering.
The upward pace of real estate prices has slowed down significantly.
In the financial markets, overall liquidity conditions are favorable and financial institutions' lending has increased sharply, led by loans to small and medium-sized enterprises.
Meanwhile, the current account has recorded a deficit recently owing mainly to the narrowed goods account surplus and the repatriation of dividends.
Consumer price inflation and core inflation both remain stable.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
